alignments.note: Temporal בְּ + infinitive construct recast as a finite temporal clause; the preposition takes the *when* (rule 52).
Infinitive construct keeps the verb; *forth* is the phrasal particle completing the going-out lexeme (rule 44), head on *went*.
Subject of the infinitive, reordered before the verb in English.
מִן → *out of*, headed on *out* which carries the ablative lexeme (rule 24).
Construct noun with no article morpheme takes the supplied *The* (rule 29).
Indefinite article belongs to the noun (rule 15).

Attributive participle לָעַז 'speaking a foreign tongue' recast as *of strange language*; the *of* and both words are the ASV's rendering of this one participle (rule 31), no second source nominal stands for rule 19. Headed on *strange*, which carries the foreignness; *language* is a defensible alternative head.

review_notes: Whole-verse temporal clause; no verb in the second colon, none supplied by the ASV.
